audit.why: Riven loses this lane on average over 1082 games. The mirror audit settled on EVEN / 6.5/10 for the pair, and difficulty must not contradict the win rate a paying user can see on the same page.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 6.5/10, and the two difficulty strings reworded to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Riven six of seven rows, including Level 6, first item and two items, while whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] all say Cho'Gath takes those stages.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Skill] and the mirror audit has already shipped exactly that order on Cho'Gath's side — my page must state the same facts or mirror-fix will overwrite it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs with ratings pulled in line, and the phases whys rewritten around Rupture's 6s cooldown and Feast's 80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid all state that Feast's true damage 'ignores your shield' / 'ignores your E shield, Immortal Shieldbow passive, and any sustain'.
audit.why: True damage ignores armour and magic resist. It does not ignore shields — Valor's shield absorbs true damage like any other. This tells a Riven player their defensive cooldown is worthless in the exact window where it is the thing keeping them alive. The mirror audit found the identical error on Cho'Gath's side and expects it to recur across every shield-owning enemy in his list.
audit.corrected: All three restated as 'ignores armour and MR', with Valor explicitly still absorbing it. Feast's 80s rank-1 cooldown added so the punish window is concrete.

audit.why: Rupture is 6s flat at every rank and Feral Scream 11s at rank 1 — the page's advice to trade on Rupture downtime is sound; the numbers are now stated.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a careful equilibrium — you still out-trade him if you avoid his Rupture knockup, but every Feast stack he collects on minions is compounding HP that makes your Wind Slash execute land later and later. Bait him into stepping up by holding the wave near your side, then commit when Rupture is on cooldown. At Level 6 the math changes against you: his Feast R is a true-damage execute that ignores your E shield, Immortal Shieldbow passive, and any sustain you've bought — if you try a Level 6 all-in with him above roughly 40% HP and land Wind Slash, there's a strong chance he Feasts you back while you're in a post-combo cooldown window. Force the all-in only if you have a kill-assured HP lead from earlier.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a careful equilibrium — you still out-trade him if you avoid his Rupture knockup, but every Feast stack he collects on minions is compounding HP that makes your Wind Slash execute land later and later. Bait him into stepping up by holding the wave near your side, then commit in Rupture's 6-second downtime. At Level 6 the math changes: Feast is true damage, so no amount of armour or MR helps — Valor's shield does absorb it, but if you all-in above roughly 40% HP and land Wind Slash, he Feasts you back while you sit in the post-combo cooldown window. Force the all-in only with a kill-assured HP lead from earlier.

edits.before: At 2+ items Cho'Gath becomes a problem you cannot solve in the side-lane: Feast stacks have inflated his HP to a point where your combo chip-damages him, he has enough armor and MR to absorb your burst, and his true-damage R true-damages through everything you build — there is no itemisation that answers it. Accept that the 1v1 is gone, group for teamfights where you can access his backline instead, and use your mid-game roam advantage (if you built one) to stay relevant. If the game goes past 30 minutes with Cho'Gath ahead, your job is flanking carries, not fighting him directly.
edits.after: At 2+ items Cho'Gath becomes a problem you cannot solve in the side lane: Feast stacks have inflated his HP to the point where your combo only chips him, he has enough armour and MR to absorb your burst, and Feast itself is true damage, so no resistance you buy reduces it by a point. Accept that the 1v1 is gone, group for teamfights where you can reach his backline instead, and use your mid-game roam advantage to stay relevant. If the game passes 30 minutes with Cho'Gath ahead, your job is flanking carries, not fighting him.

edits.before: Feast stacks plus a completed tank item make Cho'Gath effectively unkillable in a side-lane 1v1 — his true-damage R punches through every defensive answer Riven can build, and you lack the percent-health damage to cut through him.
edits.after: Feast stacks plus a tank item end the side-lane 1v1 for you — armour and MR do not reduce his true damage — but the stage is still a coin flip overall, because his kit contributes far less to a teamfight than your flank does.
